Prealgebra · Lesson 11.8

The Pythagorean Theorem

Solve this lesson →All lessons

In every right triangle, the three sides are connected by a rule that holds exactly, not just approximately. That rule is the Pythagorean Theorem. You will see why it has to be true using nothing but the areas of squares, then use it to find lengths you cannot measure directly.

Key idea
In a right triangle, the two sides that meet at the right angle are the legs, and the side opposite the right angle is the hypotenuse. It is always the longest side, since it is opposite the largest angle. Build a square on each side. The Pythagorean Theorem says the square on the hypotenuse equals the two squares on the legs put together, a2+b2=c2a2+b2=c2, with aa and bb the legs and cc the hypotenuse. For a 3-4-5 triangle, 9+16=259+16=25.
Problem
In the diagram above is a right triangle with legs 33 and 44. Find the hypotenuse. Give the number of units.
Show a hint
  • The hypotenuse is the side opposite the right angle. The Pythagorean Theorem says the squares of the two legs add up to the square of the hypotenuse.
  • Square each leg and add, then take the square root of that total to get the hypotenuse.
Show the full solution
Square the legs and add. c2=32+42=9+16=25c2=32+42=9+16=25, so c=25=5c=25​=5​. That is the 3-4-5 right triangle, the first one worth memorizing. Note the last step is a square root, not the sum itself.
Problem
In the diagram above is a right triangle with legs 66 and 88. Find the hypotenuse. Give the number of units.
Show a hint
  • The hypotenuse is the side across from the right angle. The Pythagorean Theorem says its square equals the sum of the squares of the two legs.
  • Square each leg and add them to get c2c2. Then take the square root to find cc.
Show the full solution
Add the squares of the legs. c2=62+82=36+64=100c2=62+82=36+64=100 Take the square root, c=100=10c=100​=10​. This is the 3-4-5 triangle with every side doubled, so you could have read the answer off without squaring anything.
Problem
In the diagram above is a right triangle with legs 55 and 1212. Find the hypotenuse. Give the number of units.
Show a hint
  • The hypotenuse cc is the side opposite the right angle. By the Pythagorean Theorem, a2+b2=c2a2+b2=c2, so square each leg and add.
  • You have c2=52+122c2=52+122. Work out the two squares, add them, then take the square root to get cc.
Show the full solution
Add the squares of the legs. c2=52+122=25+144=169c2=52+122=25+144=169 Since 132=169132=169, the hypotenuse is 1313​. The 5-12-13 triangle is worth memorizing right alongside 3-4-5.
Key idea
Here is a visual proof. Fit four copies of the right triangle into a big square of side a+ba+b, leaving a tilted square hole of side cc in the middle. The big square has area (a+b)2(a+b)2. That same area is also the four triangles plus the hole, 4⋅12ab+c2=2ab+c24⋅21​ab+c2=2ab+c2. Since (a+b)2=a2+2ab+b2(a+b)2=a2+2ab+b2, the 2ab2ab appears on both sides and cancels, leaving a2+b2=c2a2+b2=c2.
Problem
In the diagram above is a right triangle with hypotenuse 1313 and one leg 55. The other leg is the question mark. Find the missing leg. Give the number of units.
Show a hint
  • The Pythagorean Theorem says a2+b2=c2a2+b2=c2. Here the hypotenuse is known and one leg is missing, so rearrange to b2=c2−a2b2=c2−a2 and subtract instead of add.
  • Compute 132132 and 5252, subtract, then take the square root of what is left.
Show the full solution
The hypotenuse is known here, so subtract. b2=132−52=169−25=144b2=132−52=169−25=144 Take the square root, b=144=12b=144​=12​. Looking for a leg always means subtracting the squares. These sides are the 5-12-13 triple again.
Problem
In the diagram above is a right triangle with legs 1212 and 1616. Find the hypotenuse. Give the number of units.
Show a hint
  • The Pythagorean Theorem says a2+b2=c2a2+b2=c2. Square both legs and add to get c2c2, then take the square root.
  • Look closer at 1212 and 1616. They are 44 times 33 and 44, so this is a 3-4-5 triangle scaled up by 44.
Show the full solution
Add the squares of the legs. 122+162=144+256=400122+162=144+256=400 Take the square root, c=400=20c=400​=20​. Faster route, 1212 and 1616 are 44 times 33 and 44, so this is a 3-4-5 triangle scaled by 44 and the hypotenuse is 4×54×5.
Problem
In the diagram above is a right triangle with legs 88 and 1515. Find the hypotenuse. Give the number of units.
Show a hint
  • The hypotenuse squared equals the sum of the squares of the legs, so c2=82+152c2=82+152.
  • Add 64+22564+225, then take the square root of that total.
Show the full solution
Add the squares of the legs. c2=82+152=64+225=289c2=82+152=64+225=289 Take the square root, c=289=17c=289​=17​. Add 8-15-17 to your list of whole-number triples, next to 3-4-5 and 5-12-13.
Key idea
The theorem works both ways. To find the hypotenuse, add the squares of the legs and take the root. To find a missing leg, subtract instead, using b2=c2−a2b2=c2−a2, since the leg squares add to the hypotenuse square. Adding when you want a leg gives a length longer than the hypotenuse. A right triangle with whole numbers on all three sides is a Pythagorean triple, like 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17, and any multiple works too (6-8-10, 9-12-15). Recognizing a triple gives the third side without arithmetic.
Problem
In the diagram above is a right triangle with hypotenuse 1717 and one leg 88. Find the missing leg. Give the number of units.
Show a hint
  • This time the hypotenuse is known and a leg is missing, so rearrange the Pythagorean Theorem to b2=c2−a2b2=c2−a2.
  • Square the hypotenuse and the known leg, subtract, then take the square root of what is left.
Show the full solution
The hypotenuse is given, so subtract. b2=172−82=289−64=225b2=172−82=289−64=225 Take the square root, b=225=15b=225​=15​. That fills in the 8-15-17 triple from the last problem, read backwards.
Problem
In the diagram above, a ladder leans against a wall. Its foot sits 77 feet from the wall, and the top reaches 2424 feet up the wall. How long is the ladder? Give the number of units.
Show a hint
  • The wall and the ground meet at a right angle, so the ladder, the ground, and the wall form a right triangle. The ladder leans across from the right angle, so it is the hypotenuse. The two legs are the 77 feet along the ground and the 2424 feet up the wall.
  • By the Pythagorean Theorem, square each leg and add them to get the square of the ladder's length, c2=72+242c2=72+242. Work that sum out, then take the square root to get cc.
Show the full solution
The ladder is the hypotenuse, and the legs are the 77 feet along the ground and the 2424 feet up the wall. c2=72+242=49+576=625c2=72+242=49+576=625 Taking the square root, the ladder is 2525​ feet long. A wall meets the ground at a right angle, so a leaning ladder is always the hypotenuse. 7-24-25 is another triple worth knowing.
Key idea
The theorem is most useful when you need a length you cannot measure directly. Think of a ladder against a wall, a wire strung between two poles, or a straight path across a park. In each case the slanted length is the hypotenuse of a right triangle whose two legs you can measure. Pace out one leg along the ground, read the other up the wall or pole, then square them, add, and take the root.
Problem
In the diagram above, the tops of two poles are joined by a straight wire. The tops differ in height by 2020 feet, and the poles stand 2121 feet apart. Find the length of the wire. Give the number of units.
Show a hint
  • The wire, the horizontal gap, and the height difference form a right triangle, with the wire as the hypotenuse. Which two lengths are the legs?
  • By the Pythagorean Theorem, square the two legs and add them, then take the square root to get the wire.
Show the full solution
The wire is the hypotenuse, with legs 2020 for the height difference and 2121 for the gap between the poles. c2=202+212=400+441=841c2=202+212=400+441=841 Taking the square root, the wire is 2929​ feet long. The poles do not need equal heights for this to work, since only the difference between the tops matters.
Problem
In the diagram above, two points sit 99 units apart horizontally and 4040 units apart vertically. The straight line between them is the hypotenuse of a right triangle whose legs are those two gaps. Find the straight distance between the points. Give the number of units.
Show a hint
  • The horizontal and vertical gaps are the two legs, and the straight distance is the hypotenuse cc. Use a2+b2=c2a2+b2=c2 with the legs 99 and 4040.
  • Square each leg and add. 92=8192=81 and 402=1600402=1600, so c2=1681c2=1681. Now take the square root.
Show the full solution
The straight distance is the hypotenuse, with the horizontal and vertical gaps as the legs. By the Pythagorean Theorem, c2=92+402=81+1600=1681.c2=92+402=81+1600=1681. Taking the square root, c=1681=41c=1681​=41. So the distance is 4141​.
Problem
In the diagram above, a rectangle has a diagonal of length 2626 and one side of length 1010. Find the length of the other side. Give the number of units.
Show a hint
  • The diagonal cuts the rectangle into two right triangles. In each one the two sides of the rectangle are the legs and the diagonal is the hypotenuse.
  • You know the hypotenuse and one leg, so use b2=c2−a2b2=c2−a2 to find the missing leg.
Show the full solution
The diagonal is the hypotenuse of a right triangle whose legs are the two sides of the rectangle. To find a missing leg you subtract the squares and take the square root, 262−102=676−100=576=24.262−102​=676−100​=576​=24. So the other side is 2424​.
Fun fact
Though it carries Pythagoras's name, this relationship was known to the Babylonians more than a thousand years before he was born. Clay tablets show they were already working with whole-number right triangles. Today there are over four hundred different proofs of the theorem, and one of them was worked out by James Garfield, a future president of the United States, while he was serving in Congress.
Problem
In the diagram above is a right triangle with legs 3535 and 1212. Find the hypotenuse. Give the number of units.
Show a hint
  • The Pythagorean Theorem says the squares of the two legs add up to the square of the hypotenuse, a2+b2=c2a2+b2=c2. Square each leg and add.
  • You should have 352+122=1369352+122=1369. The hypotenuse is the square root of that. Try to spot which whole number squares to 13691369.
Show the full solution
Add the squares of the legs. c2=352+122=1225+144=1369c2=352+122=1225+144=1369 Take the square root, c=1369=37c=1369​=37​. 12-35-37 is one more whole-number triple. The two legs can be wildly different in size and the hypotenuse still comes out whole.
Problem
In the diagram above is a right triangle with hypotenuse 2525 and one leg 2020. The other leg is unknown. Find the area of the triangle. Give the number of square units.
Show a hint
  • To find the area you need a base and a height, and the two legs work perfectly. But you only know one leg, so use the Pythagorean Theorem first to get the missing one.
  • Once you have both legs, the area of a right triangle is half the product of the legs, since the legs are the base and height.
Show the full solution
Find the missing leg first. b=252−202=625−400=225=15b=252−202​=625−400​=225​=15 In a right triangle the legs are the base and height, so the area is 12×20×15=150.21​×20×15=150​. The hypotenuse is never the base or the height, which is why the missing leg has to come first.

Show the solution
The two legs are 1616 and 1212, so the hypotenuse is the square root of the sum of their squares.c=162+122=256+144=400=20c=162+122​=256+144​=400​=20So the hypotenuse is 2020​.
Practice
In the diagram above is a right triangle with legs 2424 and 77. Find the hypotenuse. Give the number of units.
Show the solution
Add the squares of the legs. c2=242+72=576+49=625c2=242+72=576+49=625 Taking the square root, c=625=25c=625​=25​. This is the 7-24-25 triangle, another whole-number triple worth recognizing on sight.
Practice
In the diagram above is a right triangle with legs 2121 and 2020. Find the hypotenuse. Give the number of units.
Show the solution
By the Pythagorean Theorem, the hypotenuse is the square root of the sum of the squares of the legs. c=212+202=441+400=841c=212+202​=441+400​=841​ Since 292=841292=841, the hypotenuse is 2929​.
Practice
In the diagram above is a right triangle with hypotenuse 2525 and one leg 2424. Find the other leg. Give the number of units.
Show the solution
Subtract to isolate the missing leg. b2=252−242=625−576=49b2=252−242=625−576=49 Take the square root, b=49=7b=49​=7​. Same 7-24-25 triangle as before, only now you are handed the hypotenuse and asked for a leg.
Practice
In the diagram above is a right triangle with hypotenuse 1515 and one leg 99. Find the missing leg. Give the number of units.
Show the solution
Since we know the hypotenuse and want a leg, we subtract. By the Pythagorean Theorem, b2=c2−a2b2=c2−a2, so b2=152−92=225−81=144.b2=152−92=225−81=144. Taking the square root, b=144=12b=144​=12. The missing leg is 1212​.
Practice
In the diagram above is a right triangle with hypotenuse 4141 and one leg 4040. Find the length of the other leg. Give the number of units.
Show the solution
Subtract the squares. b2=412−402=1681−1600=81b2=412−402=1681−1600=81 Take the square root, so the other leg is 99​ units. The sides 99, 4040, 4141 form a Pythagorean triple, and it turned up earlier in this lesson too.
Practice
In the diagram above is a right triangle with legs 2424 and 1010. Find the hypotenuse. Give the number of units.
Show the solution
The hypotenuse is the longest side, opposite the right angle. By the Pythagorean Theorem, c2=242+102c2=242+102, so c=576+100=676=26.c=576+100​=676​=26. The hypotenuse is 2626​.
Practice
In the diagram above, a ladder leans against a wall. Its foot sits 55 feet from the wall and its top reaches 1212 feet up. The ladder itself is the hypotenuse of the right triangle. How long is the ladder? Give the number of units.
Show the solution
The ladder is the hypotenuse, with legs 55 along the ground and 1212 up the wall. c2=52+122=25+144=169c2=52+122=25+144=169 Taking the square root, the ladder is 1313​ feet long. The wall meets the ground at a right angle, so a leaning ladder is always the hypotenuse. These sides are the 5-12-13 triple.
Practice
In the diagram above the two points are 88 apart horizontally and 1515 apart vertically. The straight line joining them is the hypotenuse of a right triangle whose legs are those two gaps. Find the distance between the points. Give the number of units.
Show the solution
The two gaps are the legs and the straight distance is the hypotenuse. 82+152=64+225=289=1782+152​=64+225​=289​=17 So the distance is 1717​ units. This is the 8-15-17 triple again, showing up as a distance instead of a triangle side.
Practice
In the diagram above, a wire runs from the top of one pole to the top of another. The tops differ in height by 2424 feet, and the poles stand 1818 feet apart. Find the length of the wire. Give the number of units.
Show the solution
The wire is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs 1818 and 2424, so by the Pythagorean Theorem 182+242=324+576=900.182+242=324+576=900. Take the square root, 900=30900​=30. The wire is 3030​ feet long.
Practice
The diagram above shows a rectangle with a diagonal of 3737 and one side of 1212. The diagonal cuts the rectangle into a right triangle, with the diagonal as the hypotenuse. Find the length of the other side. Give the number of units.
Show the solution
The diagonal is the hypotenuse, so the missing side is a leg. To find a leg, subtract the squares. b2=372−122=1369−144=1225.b2=372−122=1369−144=1225. Take the square root. b=1225=35b=1225​=35. The other side is 3535​ units.
Practice
In the diagram above is a right triangle with legs 4040 and 99. Find the hypotenuse. Give the number of units.
Show the solution
The hypotenuse squared equals the sum of the squares of the legs, so c2=402+92=1600+81=1681.c2=402+92=1600+81=1681. Take the square root, c=1681=41c=1681​=41. The hypotenuse is 4141​.
Practice
In the diagram above is a right triangle with hypotenuse 1717 and one leg 1515. Find the area of the triangle. Give the number of square units.
Show the solution
Find the missing leg first. b2=172−152=289−225=64,b=64=8b2=172−152=289−225=64,b=64​=8 The legs 1515 and 88 are the base and height, so the area is 12×15×8=6021​×15×8=60​ square units. Only the legs serve as base and height in a right triangle, so the hypotenuse never enters the area.
